KFGQPC Madani · ownership audit

Seventeen marks filed a page away from their word

Every diacritic in the mushaf sits on a letter. These seventeen sit roughly 300 units from the nearest letter of the word that owns them — the full width of a line. The ink is drawn correctly and is pixel-identical either way; only the grouping is wrong.

Why the distance is proof rather than a guess

Distance from each mark to the nearest letter of the word holding it, measured across all 604 pages and all 77,429 words.

0–22,735

150–31017

Nothing in the mushaf lies between 40 and 150 units from its word, and the two widest legitimate gaps are between 20 and 40. A mark 60 units clear has not drifted — it is filed under the wrong word, and no appeal to the text is needed to say so.

One cause, seventeen times

In every case the holder is the word at one end of a line and the mark is drawn at the opposite end, in the band of the line above or below. The last word of a line and the first word of the next are neighbours in reading order and a page apart on the paper — and the ownership followed the text. Each mark's own line tag is already correct; only the word is wrong. Two of the four line errors the outside reference confirmed, بِمَا on p543 and لَهَا on p599, are in this set.
